issue.title: Shadow CODEX_HOME symlinks shared codex sqlite state and sessions, causing stale rollout paths and mid-turn rollout-record failures
issue.description:
Discovered while diagnosing the 2026-09-16 silent sudo-gate failure of agent 0lw.r0 (chat gh_sase_org__sase-ace_run-0lw_r0-260916_100310). Not the cause of that failure, but a real latent defect.

`_create_shadow_codex_home` in `src/sase/llm_provider/codex.py` builds a disposable per-run CODEX_HOME under `~/.cache/sase/codex_home/<pid>-<uuid>` by copying `config.toml` and symlinking every other entry of the real `~/.codex` into it — including the mutable shared sqlite state (`state_5.sqlite` plus its `-wal`/`-shm` files, `logs_2.sqlite`, `goals_1.sqlite`, `memories_1.sqlite`), `sessions/`, and `history.jsonl`.

Consequences observed in production logs (`~/.sase/workflows/202609/gh_sase-org__sase_ace-run-260916_100310.txt`):

1. Codex records each thread's rollout path as seen through `$CODEX_HOME`, i.e. under the disposable shadow prefix. Once the shadow home is reaped, the shared state db is full of dangling paths: ~100 `ERROR codex_rollout::list: state db returned stale rollout path` lines at every codex startup (the rollout files themselves still exist under the real `~/.codex/sessions/`, so this is pure path indirection breakage).
2. Concurrent SASE codex runs (e.g. 0lv.w0--code 09:45-10:08 overlapping 0lw.r0 10:04) all write the same sqlite db through separate symlink sets. At teardown of run 0lw.r0, codex logged `ERROR codex_core::session: failed to record rollout items: thread 01a0aa88-... not found` — the run's own thread row was missing from the shared db even though its rollout file existed.

Likely remediation: stop symlinking mutable db/session state into shadow homes; let each run start with fresh empty state (codex recreates the db and sessions dir), keeping symlinks only for genuinely shared read-mostly entries (auth.json, skills, plugins, cache, installation_id, version.json). SASE agents are single-turn, so cross-run codex thread history is unused. Verify nothing in SASE reads rollouts through the shared db after teardown (transcript/thinking extraction reads while the run is live).

task_type_fields.impact: Every codex-provider agent run: noisy ERROR spam in every workflow log, shared-sqlite write races between concurrent runs, and lost rollout/thread records at teardown; risk of harder codex session corruption as concurrency grows.
task_type_fields.repro: Run any SASE codex agent and read the workflow output log: startup shows ~100 'state db returned stale rollout path' ERRORs; with two codex agents running concurrently, teardown can log 'failed to record rollout items: thread ... not found' (seen in ~/.sase/workflows/202609/gh_sase-org__sase_ace-run-260916_100310.txt). ls -la ~/.cache/sase/codex_home/<any>/ shows state_5.sqlite, sessions, history.jsonl symlinked to ~/.codex.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction 2026-09-25 (agent sase-17x.13.10.1, codex gpt-5.6-terra, artifacts ace-run/202609/25/20260925084326): 93 'codex_rollout::list: state db returned stale rollout path' ERROR lines at startup (~1.6s) were embedded verbatim in the LLMInvocationError stderr, so error_report.md grew to 39KB and its Error block opened with ~6KB of this spam, burying the real cause (an OpenAI 'Invalid prompt: flagged as potentially violating our usage policy' turn failure) until the lines were grepped out. Additional impact beyond the original report: fixing the shadow-home state sharing also restores readable failure diagnostics in error_report.md / TUI error views. 22 retained error reports contain this spam (up to 381 lines each, 2026-07-09 through 2026-09-25).
